chunks: By Allah, surely they have not gone away from oppression
And we only desire in this matter that Allah should make easy for us its hardships
and level for us its unevenness
if Allah wills; and the peace.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'they have not gone away from oppression' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This letter, attributed to Imam Ali (AS) in *Nahj al-Balagha*, critiques the Ghatafan tribe's defection to Syria during the Battle of the Camel, highlighting their preference for the ease of oppression over the rigors of justice. The Imam expresses hope that God will ease the hardships of their eventual return to the truth, reflecting the Shia theological emphasis on *tawassul* (seeking facilitation) and the inevitability of divine justice. This passage underscores the political and spiritual dynamics of the early Islamic community, where loyalty was often tested by the allure of power versus the cost of righteousness.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, surely they have not gone away from oppression
In this matter, we only desire Allāh to resolve for us its hardships
and to level for us its urneveness,
if Allāh wills; and that is an end to the matter.
